cell_line_specific_synergy: PMID 38645422 reports a clinical case of a patient with a novel FGFR2 alteration (W290_P307>C), CDKN2A/B alterations, and CDH1 alteration who received combination therapy with pazopanib + crizotinib + palbociclib after progression on pazopanib monotherapy. The patient exhibited 'a remarkable and sustained response to this innovative combination.' However, this is a single-patient case report in a human subject with specific molecular alterations, not an experiment in the UACC62 melanoma cell line (cell_line=85). The abstract does not specify the primary cancer type, dose schedules, quantification of synergy by any mathematical model (Bliss, Loewe, ZIP, HSA, or other), numerical response metrics, or comparison to expected additive effects. The rationale was multi-pathway targeting: pazopanib for FGFR2, crizotinib for synthetic lethality with CDH1, and palbociclib for CDKN2A/B. No verified PubMed record retrieved by code describes experimental combination treatment or formal synergy assessment of palbociclib + pazopanib in UACC62, any melanoma cell line, or any skin cancer model system. PMID 32576580 and PMID 30660363 report in vivo sarcoma PDOX studies testing palbociclib and pazopanib as separate monotherapy arms (not combined) in doxorubicin-resistant dedifferentiated liposarcoma and leiomyosarcoma, respectively; these are soft-tissue sarcomas, not skin cancers, and no combination or synergy data are reported. PMID 37610680 describes multi-omic profiling of an imatinib-resistant DFSP PDX model with CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion, a molecular feature that could rationalize palbociclib (CDK4/6 inhibitor) use, but this abstract does not report testing palbociclib, pazopanib, or any combination therapy. No other verified record describes experimental combination or synergy evaluation for this drug pair in skin cancer models.

cancer_pathway_or_phenotype: Hypothesis (not confirmed by retrieved literature for this exact drug pair and cancer type): Palbociclib is a selective, ATP-competitive inhibitor of cyclin-dependent kinases CDK4 and CDK6, blocking retinoblastoma (Rb) protein phosphorylation, inducing G1 cell-cycle arrest, and inhibiting proliferation; it is FDA-approved for HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer in combination with endocrine therapy. Pazopanib is a multi-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) with activity against VEGFR-1, -2, -3, PDGFR-α/β, FGFR-1, -3, KIT, and other kinases; it inhibits angiogenesis and tumor growth and is FDA-approved for renal cell carcinoma and soft-tissue sarcoma. Generic pathway logic suggests that cell-cycle inhibition (palbociclib) and multi-kinase inhibition targeting angiogenic and growth-factor signaling (pazopanib) could affect distinct or partially overlapping cellular processes. PMID 38645422 (clinical case, not UACC62) describes rational multi-pathway targeting: pazopanib for FGFR2 alteration, palbociclib for CDKN2A/B alterations (loss of CDK4/6 negative regulators p16INK4a and p15INK4b, conferring potential palbociclib sensitivity). PMID 37610680 describes CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion in a DFSP PDX model, a genomic alteration that could rationalize CDK4/6 inhibitor use, but does not test palbociclib or pazopanib. PMID 32576580 and PMID 30660363 test palbociclib and pazopanib as separate monotherapy arms in sarcoma PDOX models (not skin cancer, not combined). No verified record directly links palbociclib + pazopanib combination to a specific pathway mechanism or phenotype in melanoma or skin cancer.
mechanistic_rationale: PMID 38645422 provides a multi-pathway targeting rationale for the combination pazopanib + crizotinib + palbociclib in a patient with FGFR2, CDH1, and CDKN2A/B alterations: pazopanib was selected to target the FGFR2 alteration (pazopanib has FGFR-1 and FGFR-3 inhibitory activity per its known TKI profile, though FGFR2 is not typically listed as a primary pazopanib target), crizotinib for synthetic lethality with CDH1 alteration, and palbociclib for CDKN2A/B loss (loss of CDK4/6 inhibitors p16INK4a/p15INK4b). However, this is a three-drug combination in a clinical case with specific molecular alterations, not a mechanistic study of palbociclib + pazopanib in UACC62 melanoma. PMID 37610680 describes CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion in a DFSP model, a genomic context where palbociclib might paradoxically be less effective (loss of negative regulators can confer resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors in some contexts, though results vary by cancer type and co-alterations). No verified record provides direct mechanistic rationale or experimental data for synergy of palbociclib + pazopanib in skin cancer models.
evidence_summary: No verified PubMed record retrieved by code reports experimental combination treatment or quantified synergy assessment for palbociclib (CID 5330286) + pazopanib (CID 10113978) in the UACC62 melanoma cell line (cell_line=85) or any skin cancer model. PMID 38645422 is a clinical case report describing a patient with a novel FGFR2 alteration, CDKN2A/B alterations, and CDH1 alteration who received a three-drug combination (pazopanib + crizotinib + palbociclib) after progression on pazopanib monotherapy and achieved 'a remarkable and sustained response.' This provides clinical evidence that the combination can be administered and may produce clinical benefit in a genetically defined patient, but it is: (1) a single-patient case, not a controlled experiment; (2) a three-drug regimen, not the two-drug pair specified; (3) in a patient with a specific, rare molecular context (FGFR2, CDH1, CDKN2A/B alterations), not UACC62 melanoma; (4) lacking quantified synergy assessment (no Bliss, Loewe, ZIP, HSA, or other model reported); and (5) does not specify the primary cancer type in the abstract. PMID 32576580 and PMID 30660363 test palbociclib and pazopanib as separate monotherapy arms in sarcoma PDOX models (dedifferentiated liposarcoma and leiomyosarcoma, respectively), not in combination and not in skin cancer. PMID 37610680 describes multi-omic profiling of an imatinib-resistant DFSP PDX with CDKN2A/B deletion but does not report testing palbociclib, pazopanib, or any combination. Multiple verified records (PMID 27126828, PMID 34022396, PMID 38968741, PMID 35267464, PMID 36750444, PMID 35656880, PMID 35178745) mention palbociclib and/or pazopanib in review, pharmacokinetic, or formulation contexts but provide no experimental combination or synergy data. The computational screen metadata (z_HSA=3.11, HSA_GT=31.4, label=synergy) indicates a computational prediction for UACC62, but this is a screen output, not published experimental literature evidence.
negative_or_contradictory_evidence: No verified PubMed record retrieved by code reports negative, antagonistic, or contradictory results for palbociclib + pazopanib combination in UACC62, melanoma, or skin cancer models. PMID 37610680 describes CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion in a DFSP model; loss of CDK4/6 negative regulators (p16INK4a, p15INK4b) can, in some cellular contexts, confer resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors such as palbociclib, though the functional consequence depends on Rb status and other co-alterations. The abstract does not report testing palbociclib or pazopanib, so no direct contradictory data are available. No record contradicts the plausibility of the combination, but the absence of published experimental data precludes assessment of negative results.
cell_line_model_limitations: UACC62 is a human melanoma cell line; verified literature provides no experimental data on palbociclib + pazopanib combination in this line. PMID 38645422 describes a clinical case in a human patient, not a cell line model, and the three-drug combination response in a patient with rare molecular alterations (FGFR2, CDH1, CDKN2A/B) cannot be extrapolated to UACC62 melanoma without knowledge of UACC62's molecular profile and direct experimental validation. PMID 37610680 describes a DFSP PDX and cell line model (MDFSP-S1) with CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion and COL1A1-PDGFB fusion; this is a dermatofibrosarcoma model, not melanoma, and no combination data are reported. PMID 32576580 and PMID 30660363 use patient-derived orthotopic xenograft (PDOX) models of sarcomas (dedifferentiated liposarcoma, leiomyosarcoma), not melanoma or skin cancer, and test palbociclib and pazopanib as separate monotherapy arms. General limitations of in vitro cell line models (lack of tumor microenvironment, stromal cells, immune components, angiogenesis) apply but are not directly addressed by the retrieved corpus for UACC62. The single clinical case (PMID 38645422) provides human in vivo context but involves a genetically distinct tumor, a three-drug regimen, and no controlled synergy quantification.
